current_host_observation.volume_grouping_method: lstat st_dev for each named recovery-root entry; identifiers are local to this boot and are not volume identity pins
current_host_observation.status_source: read-only tools/brain_host_recovery.py status plus df and diskutil apfs listSnapshots

offline_route_capability_observation.macos_recovery_available_on_current_arch: Apple documents macOS Recovery, Terminal, and Share Disk for Apple silicon; this is product documentation, not a rehearsal
offline_route_capability_observation.manual_source: local macOS diskutil(8); checked with man diskutil on the observed host
offline_route_capability_observation.unlock_nomount_applicability: only if the Data volume is encrypted and locked

feasibility.live_non_snapshot_owner_wide_cutoff: not credible while the recorded owner services remain active and prior metadata scans showed owner-state churn
feasibility.offline_readonly_data_view: conditionally feasible candidate; requires orderly shutdown, Recovery/offline boot, explicit Data identity verification, unlock without mounting, explicit read-only mount, and post-mount read-only verification
feasibility.same_st_dev_root_entries_observed: the lstat metadata for the named owner/research/config/LaunchAgent root entries reported the same local device as internal Data; entry type, symlink/alias targets, descendants, and their volume placement were not proven

required_acceptance_evidence: User-controlled orderly shutdown completed before the capture environment starts; no source-host services are running, and independent evidence establishes that no writable Data mount occurred in Recovery before the chosen source-view boundary.
Exact APFS Data volume UUID, volume-group/container/device identity, and every source root are bound to the same intended Data volume; any root on another volume is separately assigned or unresolved.
If Data is encrypted and locked, unlock it interactively without mounting first; no passphrase is placed in argv, logs, or receipts.

Data is mounted explicitly read-only at a recorded mountpoint; mount source and filesystem flags are checked before and after capture, including held descriptor identity and filesystem read-only state.
All source roots remain within the held read-only Data view; no live alias, firmlink, external mount, unresolved symlink, or unassigned protected root bypasses that view.
A trusted pinned capture tool and required runtime are available offline from Kingston or another declared source; the tool has no activation or provider-request path.
The capture receipt binds the shutdown/source-view boundary, source volume and root identities, exclusions, failures, and the separate Kingston K frontier without converting unknown or pending state.
abort_conditions: Data identity mismatch, any required root outside the approved source view, or inability to prove all held roots share the intended volume.
The mount is writable, mount source is ambiguous, volume must be repaired or replayed, or any source writer can still mutate the Data volume.
Capture tool/runtime is unavailable or unpinned, or capture requires installing software to the source Data volume.
Protected-root closure, SQLite/application-consistency handling, or metadata/ACL/xattr preservation remains unresolved for the declared scope.
limitations: The current-host st_dev grouping is an observation only; st_dev is not a portable APFS UUID and does not prove source-view identity.
This feasibility pass did not boot Recovery, unlock or mount Data, perform capture, inspect protected paths, or verify the proposed read-only workflow on this host.
Apple Share Disk documentation describes transfer but does not establish a read-only export; it is not accepted as a source-view proof.

A whole-volume read-only view can establish a stable byte view only after a qualified offline mount; it does not itself close semantic root classification, SQLite restore behavior, Kingston K lineage, or host restore.
The observed st_dev value belongs to each named root entry; it does not prove the entry is a real directory, exclude an alias or firmlink, or assign its descendants to that same volume.
